[[File:Alfred P. Wolf Los Alamos ID.png|thumb|Alfred P. Wolf c. 1941.]]
'''Alfred P. Wolf''' (February 13, 1923 – December 17, 1998) was an American nuclear and [[organic chemist]].
<ref name="NYT">{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/12/27/nyregion/alfred-p-wolf-75-chemist-who-created-imaging-tools.html|title=Alfred P. Wolf, 75, Chemist Who Created Imaging Tools|first=Wolfgang|last=Saxon|date=27 December 1998|accessdate=28 March 2019|website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>
<ref name="NAP">{{cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/publications/biographical-memoirs/|title=Biographical Memoirs Home|website=Nasonline.org|access-date=28 March 2019}}</ref>
<ref name="BROOKHAVEN">{{cite web|url=https://www.bnl.gov/bnlweb/pubaf/pr/1998/bnlpr121898.html|title=Al Wolf Obituary|website=Bnl.gov|accessdate=28 March 2019|archive-date=6 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170506181330/https://www.bnl.gov/bnlweb/pubaf/pr/1998/bnlpr121898.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
<ref name="NYU">{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/12/19/classified/paid-notice-deaths-wolf-alfred-p-phd.html|title=Paid Notice: Deaths WOLF, ALFRED P., PH.D.|date=19 December 1998|accessdate=28 March 2019|website=[[The New York Times]]}}</ref>
<ref name="JNF">{{cite journal |title=In memoriam: Alfred P. Wolf, PhD, 1923-1998 |journal=The Journal of Nuclear Medicine }}</ref>
Wolf was chairman of the Chemistry Department at [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]],<ref name="NAP"/> research professor in the Department of Psychiatry at [[New York University]]<ref name="NYU"/>
a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]],<ref name="NAP"/>
The Journal of Nuclear Medicine said that his "discoveries were instrumental in the development of [[positron emission tomography]] (PET)" and that he "made pioneering contributions over nearly 50 years in the field of organic radiochemistry".<ref name="JNF"/> ''[[The New York Times]]'' said that Wolf "helped create some of today's most sophisticated diagnostic tools" and that he "advanced the field of organic [[radiochemistry]], [[radiopharmacology]] and [[nuclear medicine]]" throughout his career of 50 years.<ref name="NYT" />
The [[National Academy of Sciences]] said that "he pioneered the development of labeling techniques that used the reactions of hot atoms".<ref name="NAP"/>

== Notable awards and distinctions ==
* 1971 the Nuclear Chemistry Award of the [[American Chemical Society]]<ref name="NAP"/>
* 1981 the [[Society of Nuclear Medicine]] [[Paul Aebersold]] Award<ref name="NAP"/>
* 1983 an [[Honorary degree|honorary doctorate]] from the Faculty of Mathematics and Science at [[Uppsala University]], [[Sweden]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uu.se/en/about-uu/traditions/prizes/honorary-doctorates/|title=Honorary doctorates - Uppsala University, Sweden|first=David|last=Naylor|website=Uu.se|accessdate=28 March 2019}}</ref>
* 1988 elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="NAP"/>
* 1991 the Hevesy Nuclear Medicine Pioneer Award<ref name="NAP"/>
* 1997 the Melvin Calvin Award of the International Isotope Society<ref name="NAP"/>

== Life and career ==
* 1923: born in [[Manhattan]] on February 13, 1923
* 1944: B.A., chemistry, [[Columbia University]]<ref name="NAP"/>
* 1948: M.A., chemistry, [[Columbia University]]<ref name="NAP"/>
* 1951: joined the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]]<ref name="NAP"/>
* 1952: Ph.D., chemistry, [[Columbia University]]<ref name="NAP"/>
* 1957: senior chemist, the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]]<ref name="NAP"/>
* 1982: head of the Chemistry Department, the [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]]<ref name="NAP"/>
